explainedBy: The hosts name Joe Camber as the fatal flaw in the chain of events at the farm.

storyboard.claim: Joe Camber is the first point of failure in the tragedy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe Camber alone in the barn workshop, neutral, naming him as the flaw.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the Camber farm section.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the blame on a named man in his workplace, not on the dog.
storyboard.staging: Joe is the subject, held still in his workshop.

explainedBy: Joe stubbornly refuses to wire a phone extension into his garage workshop.

storyboard.claim: Joe refuses a phone line in his workshop.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe, angry, beside the dead-phone icon: a handset with a red line through it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Joe as the flaw to the specific choice that is the flaw.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dead-phone icon shows the missing line; the anger shows his stubbornness.
storyboard.staging: Joe refuses the line: the dead handset is the thing he will not install.

explainedBy: Joe makes his wife or son run messages out to him from the house instead of using a phone.

storyboard.claim: Joe routes all contact through people running errands.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe, neutral, pointing out of the barn toward the house.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The missing phone line means a person carries messages instead.
storyboard.addedInformation: The point shows he sends others to the house; the icon is dropped so the line stays the deadPhone of the beat before.
storyboard.staging: Joe points toward the house he sends people from.

explainedBy: A phone extension in the barn might have let Vic reach him earlier, or let Donna hear it ring out.

storyboard.claim: A barn phone line would have changed who could reach whom.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe, worried, next to the dead-phone handset: the line that was never wired.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the refusal to what the missing line would have changed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the counterfactual: a line in the barn is what was missing.
storyboard.staging: The dead handset stands for the absent extension; Joe's worry marks what it cost.

explainedBy: A ring in the barn would have told Donna that nobody was home, changing her decision.

storyboard.claim: A ring in the barn would have told Donna the truth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Donna, worried, in the kitchen, with the callout that nobody was home.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the missing line to the knowledge it would have given Donna.
storyboard.addedInformation: The knowledge a ring would give, staged on the person who needed it.
storyboard.staging: Donna is the one the ring would have informed.

explainedBy: The hosts reject the hardware explanation and name Vic's psychology as the real flaw.
noVisual: Software is a metaphor for trust and psychology; nothing in the vocabulary shows a mind's software.

storyboard.claim: The real flaw is Vic's psychology, not the wiring.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Vic, worried, in the kitchen, with the callout on his psychology.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the phone line to the trust that decides how a missed call is read.
storyboard.addedInformation: Moves the cause from the hardware to Vic himself.
storyboard.staging: Vic is the subject; the metaphor is carried by the callout.

explainedBy: A missed call late at night means an emergency only if trust holds: the chain starts with the missed call.

storyboard.claim: A missed call is read through trust.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow starting with a single box: MISSED CALL.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Vic himself to the event his psychology reads.
storyboard.addedInformation: Starts the chain the next beats build: the missed call is the trigger.
storyboard.staging: The flow begins on the trigger, a missed call.

explainedBy: Because of the affair, the same missed call is translated into a different reading.

storyboard.claim: The affair changes how the missed call is read.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow: UNANSWERED CALL, kept on the same frame.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same chain: the missed call stays the trigger while its reading changes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Holds the chain while the narration says the call is translated.
storyboard.staging: The stage stays as it is; only the narration changes.

explainedBy: The missed call translates immediately into she abandoned me for her lover.

storyboard.claim: A missed call is read as abandonment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow grows one box: MISSED CALL then ABANDONED ME.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the reading the affair gives the call.
storyboard.addedInformation: The second step of the chain: the reading that replaces the emergency.
storyboard.staging: Second box drawn in as the chain continues.

explainedBy: Because he is embarrassed and assumes she left, he waits, and the chain ends in days of waiting.

storyboard.claim: Vic waits instead of calling the police.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The flow grows the third box: WAITS FOR DAYS.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the result the reading produces.
storyboard.addedInformation: The result of the chain: the police are not called for days.
storyboard.staging: Third box drawn in; the chain is complete.

explainedBy: The missed call becomes the trap Donna is in, because Vic does not trust her.
noVisual: The padlock on Donna's cage is a metaphor for distrust trapping her; nothing in the vocabulary draws a trap that is not a physical object.

storyboard.claim: Distrust turns a missed call into a trap for Donna.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same three-box flow: UNANSWERED CALL, ABANDONED ME, WAITS FOR DAYS.
storyboard.onScreenText: UNANSWERED CALL, ABANDONED ME, WAITS FOR DAYS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same chain; the narration widens it to Donna's situation.
storyboard.addedInformation: The metaphor is not drawn; the chain still carries the mechanism.
storyboard.staging: The stage holds the full chain; no new object is added.

explainedBy: Vic does not look for Donna, which the trust chain predicts.

storyboard.claim: Vic does not search for Donna.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Vic, neutral, in the kitchen, with the callout that he does not look for her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the chain of reading to the action it produces.
storyboard.addedInformation: The inaction is the consequence of the chain.
storyboard.staging: Vic stays in place; the callout names the failure to search.

explainedBy: Kujo is a lethal threat that nobody in his family or neighbourhood recognizes for days.

storyboard.claim: Kujo is a lethal threat nobody recognized.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo, angry, on the street, with the callout: a lethal threat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Vic's inaction to the dog nobody reads as dangerous.
storyboard.addedInformation: The threat the narration asks about, shown as the dog itself.
storyboard.staging: Kujo is the threat; his angry face is the danger the family misses.

explainedBy: Gary Pervier, the nearest neighbour, is introduced as an aging, cynical veteran and heavy drinker.

storyboard.claim: Gary is the neighbour who should have noticed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gary, neutral, on the street, with the callout naming him a cynical veteran.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the dog to the neighbour who knows it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces Gary as the one who failed to see the threat.
storyboard.staging: Gary stands as the person introduced.

explainedBy: Gary sits drunk on his porch in a broken lawn chair sinking into the weeds.

storyboard.claim: Gary is drunk and sunk in his own neglect.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gary, blank, seated in a broken lawn chair, with the callout about the weeds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the introduction to the picture of him sitting.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chair and weeds show the neglect; the blank face shows the drunken numbness.
storyboard.staging: Gary sits in the chair; the callout names the sinking.

explainedBy: Gary tosses bone-shaped dog biscuits to Kujo, feeding the dog that is sick.

storyboard.claim: Gary feeds the sick dog.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gary reaches toward Kujo, the food icon in front of him, Kujo angry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Gary's chair to his act toward the dog.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the act of feeding the dog that is ill.
storyboard.staging: Gary reaches with the biscuits; Kujo watches.

explainedBy: Kujo's eyes are red and filmy: a visible sign of the illness.

storyboard.claim: Kujo's eyes show he is sick.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo, sad, close on the street, with the callout about red and filmy eyes.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Gary feeding him to the sickness he is feeding.
storyboard.addedInformation: The eyes are the visible sign the narration names.
storyboard.staging: Kujo's sad face, the callout names the eyes.

explainedBy: Kujo's chest makes a constant low, unnatural rumble, a sign that he is very sick and dangerous.

storyboard.claim: Kujo's rumble signals illness and threat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo, angry, with the callout about the rumble in his chest.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From his eyes to the sound of his chest.
storyboard.addedInformation: The rumble is the danger the sound would carry.
storyboard.staging: Kujo's angry face, the callout names the rumble.

explainedBy: Kujo thinks about attacking Gary, yet Gary reaches out to pat the dog on the head.

storyboard.claim: Gary reaches toward the dog that threatens him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gary reaches toward Kujo, who is angry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the dog's sickness to Gary's naive act toward it.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reaching hand is the blind act the narration describes.
storyboard.staging: Gary reaches; Kujo is the threat he cannot see.

explainedBy: Gary cannot see the monster sitting two feet in front of him.

storyboard.claim: Gary is blind to the threat in front of him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gary, blank, beside angry Kujo, with the callout that he cannot see the monster.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the reach to the blindness it shows.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blank face is the blindness; the angry dog is what he cannot see.
storyboard.staging: Gary stands blank, Kujo angry beside him.

explainedBy: Our comforting memories overlay the present danger in our minds.
noVisual: The claim is general: memory overlaying present danger has no object or face in the vocabulary.

storyboard.claim: Memory overlays the present danger in everyone's mind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No person: the callout COMFORTING MEMORIES on the street.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Gary's blindness to the general mechanism behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the general mechanism; no figure is added for a general claim.
storyboard.staging: Callout only; the claim is not a person's act.

explainedBy: Gary sees the goofy dog he has known for five years, the friendly memory that blinds him.

storyboard.claim: Gary sees the dog he has known for years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gary and Kujo, both happy: the friendly dog of memory.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the general mechanism to Gary's memory of this dog.
storyboard.addedInformation: The happy dog is the memory Gary sees instead of the threat.
storyboard.staging: The friendly pair is the memory; the next beat breaks it.

explainedBy: Gary's brain refuses the new data, the red eyes and the growl, because accepting it would shatter his memory.

storyboard.claim: The new data is refused; the dog turns threatening.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Gary neutral, Kujo angry: the same pair, the dog's face changed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage: Kujo's face turns from happy to angry, and Gary's face stays blank.
storyboard.addedInformation: The dog's change is the new data the narration says Gary refuses.
storyboard.staging: Only the faces change on the kept stage.

explainedBy: Kujo's owner Joe Camber makes the same fatal error about his own dog.

storyboard.claim: Joe makes the same error as Gary.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe, worried, in the garage, with the callout about the same error.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Gary's blindness to Joe's, the owner.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes clear the owner is the one with the most at stake.
storyboard.staging: Joe is the subject in the garage.

explainedBy: Joe walks into his garage and sees massive, sickly dog droppings on the floor: the destruction.

storyboard.claim: Joe enters and sees the sign of the illness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe walks into the garage, worried, with the callout about the droppings on the floor.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the owner's error to the evidence he walks into.
storyboard.addedInformation: The droppings are the sign of the illness the narration names.
storyboard.staging: Joe walks in; the callout names the evidence.

explainedBy: Joe realizes with cold horror that his dog has contracted rabies.

storyboard.claim: Joe realizes what the evidence means.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe, afraid, beside the lightbulb icon: the idea arrives.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the evidence he walked in on to the realization it produces.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lightbulb reads as the realization; the afraid face shows the horror.
storyboard.staging: Joe is afraid; the lightbulb is the moment of understanding.

explainedBy: Joe knows intellectually that his dog has rabies, yet the knowledge does not change what he does.

storyboard.claim: Joe knows the dog has rabies.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe, afraid, with the lightbulb kept on screen and the callout HIS DOG HAS RABIES.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage: the realization is kept; the callout names what it is.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the diagnosis the realization reached.
storyboard.staging: Kept stage: the lightbulb holds the realization.

explainedBy: Kujo suddenly lunges out of the dark shadows covered in dried blood and foam.

storyboard.claim: Kujo attacks out of the dark.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo lunges at Joe, angry; Joe afraid, drawn in the same fight pose.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Joe's realization to the attack he could not avoid.
storyboard.addedInformation: The attack is the event the realization was about.
storyboard.staging: Kujo leads the lunge; Joe is drawn into it.

explainedBy: Joe's ingrained reflex makes him reach out to the attacking dog as if it were a pet.

storyboard.claim: Joe's reflex is to reach out to the dog.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Joe reaches his hand out toward Kujo, angry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the lunge to the reflex that betrays Joe.
storyboard.addedInformation: The reaching hand is the reflex the narration names.
storyboard.staging: Joe reaches; Kujo is the threat he reaches toward.

explainedBy: Right as the dog rips Joe's throat out, the reflex is over and the attack has taken him.

storyboard.claim: The dog attacks and kills Joe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo attacks Joe in a fight pose, angry; Joe drawn afraid in the same struggle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Joe's reach to the attack the reach led to.
storyboard.addedInformation: The attack ends the reflex; the death is not drawn literally.
storyboard.staging: Kujo attacks; no blood or death scene is drawn.

storyboard.concreteVisual: A refute diagram: the defense's claim, drunkenness, feeding dulled senses.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the chain of blindness to the common explanation the hosts give for it.

explainedBy: Gary is a hardcore alcoholic and Joe was drinking heavily that day, so both inputs of the claim are present.

explainedBy: The real reason is human nature: a textbook psychological phenomenon called normalcy bias.

storyboard.claim: The real model is normalcy bias, not intoxication.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same refute diagram: the reason and the correct model, normalcy bias, are drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same diagram; the correct model replaces the claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the correct psychological model the narration gives.
storyboard.staging: Kept diagram; the truth is drawn in place of the claim.

explainedBy: Brett, who is not drunk, notices that Kujo looks sick before the bus trip.
noVisual: Brett is not in the story-bible cast; the picture shows the dog he notices.

storyboard.claim: Brett sees the dog is sick.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo, worried, with the callout that he looks gross and sick.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the reasoning about drink to a sober witness.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the dog Brett noticed; the witness is named in the callout only.
storyboard.staging: Kujo is the thing noticed.

explainedBy: Kujo shows red painful eyes and lack of appetite, the sluggish signs Brett sees.

storyboard.claim: Kujo's sickness is visible.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo, sad, with the callout about lack of appetite.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the notice to the signs he sees.
storyboard.addedInformation: The lack of appetite is the sign the narration lists.
storyboard.staging: Kujo's sad face carries the sign.

explainedBy: Brett tells himself the dog ate poison bait or has a stomach bug, talking himself out of the danger.

storyboard.claim: Brett rationalizes the sickness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Kujo, neutral, with the callout listing the two excuses.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the signs to the excuses that explain them away.
storyboard.addedInformation: The two excuses the narration names.
storyboard.staging: Kujo stays neutral; the callout holds the excuses.

callout.text: BRETT HIDES IT FROM HIS DAD

explainedBy: Brett avoids telling his dad because the dad might cancel the trip to see the aunt.
noVisual: Brett and his dad are not in the story-bible cast; the callout carries the avoidance.

storyboard.claim: Brett hides the illness from his father.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A family icon, worried, with the callout naming Brett and his father.
storyboard.onScreenText: BRETT HIDES IT FROM HIS DAD
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the excuses to the secret they protect.
storyboard.addedInformation: The hidden fear: the trip would be cancelled.
storyboard.staging: The dog is the reason for the secret; the callout names the avoidance.

explainedBy: Brett, completely sober, normalizes the horror because acknowledging it would disrupt his ordinary life.
noVisual: Brett is not in the story-bible cast and normalizing an event has no vocabulary object; the callout alone carries it.

storyboard.claim: Brett normalizes the horror.
storyboard.concreteVisual: No person: the callout NORMALIZES THE HORROR in the room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the secret to the summary of the whole passage.
storyboard.addedInformation: Closes the passage on the sober witness who still did not act.
